title: Efficient Image and Media Loading
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of efficient image and media loading in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Efficient Image and Media Loading” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with responsive image selection, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Professional pages need to load efficiently, validate cleanly, adapt to different contexts, and remain understandable to other developers.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Responsive image selection lets the browser choose an appropriate resource for the viewport and pixel density. Provide a valid fallback image and verify every referenced file or URL.

items.title: Responsive image selection
items.text: Responsive image selection lets the browser choose an appropriate resource for the viewport and pixel density. Provide a valid fallback image and verify every referenced file or URL.

items.title: Lazy loading images and iframes
items.text: The loading attribute: the requested loading strategy; lazy-load off-screen media, not the primary image needed immediately.

items.title: Image dimensions and layout stability
items.text: Image dimensions and layout stability is one of the decisions covered by Efficient Image and Media Loading. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Preloading critical resources
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

items.title: Prioritizing important images
items.text: Prioritizing important images is one of the decisions covered by Efficient Image and Media Loading. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Avoiding excessive embedded media
items.text: Embedded content introduces a separate resource and sometimes a separate browsing context. Confirm the origin, disclose third-party dependencies, and restrict capabilities unless they are required.

items.title: Measuring the effect of markup changes

Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates efficient image and media loading. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Efficient Image and Media Loading.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Efficient Image and Media Loading is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
